_comment: Study A retrodiction dataset (Sprint 22, design doc 4.1). All poll values authored from model knowledge are CANDIDATES until verified=true; confidence is authorship confidence, not poll quality. observed_shift_pp = after_value - before_value. Every event here predates the LLM cutoff, so blinding_regime is sim_delta_isolated throughout.

events.event_summary: A magnitude-9.0 earthquake and tsunami devastate northeastern Japan. Explosions and core meltdowns at the Fukushima Daiichi nuclear plant force mass evacuations as radioactive contamination spreads into the air and sea; engineers battle for weeks to cool the wrecked reactors.
events.question: Will a complete phase-out of nuclear power be supported?
events.metric: % supporting a complete nuclear phase-out in Germany
events.verification_note: Infratest: phase-out support 62% (Aug 2010) -> 71% (Mar 14 2011), via Springer G-GEPON/DIW citations. Originally authored as an unverifiable 'continued use 40->26' series; switched to the verified phase-out metric.
events.notes: Referent-inversion hard case: a negative event RAISES support for the questioned subject (phase-out). A sentiment-sign mechanism is expected to miss this.

events.event_summary: Hijacked airliners are flown into the World Trade Center towers and the Pentagon, killing thousands. Both towers collapse on live television; U.S. airspace is shut down and the nation braces for further attacks.
events.question: Will the public approve of President George W. Bush's job performance?
events.metric: % approving of President G.W. Bush's job performance
events.verification_note: Gallup (news.gallup.com/poll/4912): Sept 7-10 poll 51%, Sept 14-15 poll 86% — largest rally in Gallup history.
events.notes: Classic rally-round-the-flag: strongly negative event text, sharply positive approval shift. Deliberate hard case for a sentiment-sign mechanism.

events.event_summary: A U.S.-led coalition launches a massive air campaign against Iraqi forces occupying Kuwait. Waves of airstrikes hit Baghdad as the region plunges into open war and oil markets convulse.
events.question: Will the public approve of President George H. W. Bush's job performance?
events.metric: % approving of President G.H.W. Bush's job performance
events.verification_note: Gallup retrospective (news.gallup.com/opinion/gallup/234971): 64% week before military action; 89% in March 1991, then-record high.

events.event_summary: The United States launches the invasion of Iraq with airstrikes on Baghdad and a ground push from Kuwait. Explosions light up the capital as a long, uncertain war begins against fierce international controversy.
events.question: Will the public approve of President George W. Bush's job performance?
events.metric: % approving of President G.W. Bush's job performance
events.verification_note: Gallup (news.gallup.com/poll/8074 'Iraq War Triggers Major Rally Effect'): 58% -> 71%, among the five largest rallies since WWII.

events.event_summary: President Gerald Ford grants Richard Nixon a full and unconditional pardon for all federal crimes he may have committed as president, shielding him from any Watergate prosecution and igniting accusations of a corrupt bargain.
events.question: Will the public approve of President Gerald Ford's job performance?
events.metric: % approving of President Ford's job performance
events.verification_note: Gallup retrospective (news.gallup.com/poll/23995): first reading 71%, fell to 50% in late September 1974 after the pardon.
events.notes: One of the sharpest documented single-event approval collapses.

events.event_summary: Argentine forces invade and occupy the Falkland Islands. Britain assembles a naval task force and sails to retake the islands; weeks of naval and air battles follow until Argentine forces surrender in June.
events.question: Will the public be satisfied with Prime Minister Margaret Thatcher's performance?
events.metric: % satisfied with Thatcher as Prime Minister
events.verification_note: Ipsos-MORI via UPI retrospective: 25% satisfied Jan 1982 (post-war nadir record), 59% satisfied June 1982 after recapture. Window wider than ideal (Jan baseline predates the Apr 2 invasion by 3 months).
events.notes: Some series put the immediate pre-invasion figure in the low 30s; the verified endpoints are used.

events.event_summary: President Kennedy reveals that the Soviet Union has placed nuclear missiles in Cuba and orders a naval quarantine of the island. The superpowers stand at the brink of nuclear war for thirteen days before Moscow agrees to withdraw the missiles.
events.question: Will the public approve of President John F. Kennedy's job performance?
events.metric: % approving of President Kennedy's job performance
events.verification_note: Gallup (news.gallup.com/poll/6979): 61% Oct 19-24 1962, 74% mid-November.

events.event_summary: Gunmen storm the Paris offices of the satirical magazine Charlie Hebdo, murdering journalists and police officers. Linked attacks over the following days include a hostage siege at a kosher supermarket; millions later march in unity rallies across France.
events.question: Will the public approve of President Francois Hollande's performance?
events.metric: % holding a favorable opinion of President Hollande
events.verification_note: Ifop via France24/Newsweek: 19% -> 40%, a +21pp jump — the largest in French polling history (broke Mitterrand's +19 record). Corrected from authored 21->29.

events.event_summary: Coordinated terrorist attacks strike Paris: suicide bombings at the Stade de France, mass shootings at cafes, and a massacre at the Bataclan concert hall kill 130 people. France declares a state of emergency and launches airstrikes in response.
events.question: Will the public approve of President Francois Hollande's performance?
events.metric: % holding a favorable opinion of President Hollande
events.verification_note: Ifop/JDD via France24: 20% (Oct) -> 27% (Nov). Other pollsters saw larger bounces (TNS Sofres 15->35 by Dec; Ifop/Fiducial 28->50) — the conservative single-pollster series is used.

events.event_summary: A faction of the Turkish military attempts a coup: jets bomb the parliament in Ankara, tanks block Istanbul bridges, and soldiers fire on crowds. Citizens flood the streets to resist; by morning the coup collapses with hundreds dead.
events.question: Will the public approve of President Recep Tayyip Erdogan's performance?
events.metric: % approving of President Erdogan's performance
events.verification_note: Metropoll via Bloomberg/AFP: 67.6% (Jul 28-Aug 1 2016), a rise of 21 points over the late-June poll (=46.6%). Authored 47->68 matched within rounding.

events.event_summary: As coronavirus deaths mount, the United Kingdom enters a national lockdown: the Prime Minister orders people to stay at home, closes shops and schools, and bans public gatherings while the health service braces for the surge.
events.question: Will the public approve of Prime Minister Boris Johnson's performance?
events.metric: % viewing Johnson favorably / approving of his handling
events.verification_note: YouGov via Fortune/CBC: 46% doing well (Mar 16) -> 66% (Apr 13 2020). Authored values exact.
events.notes: Early-pandemic rally seen across most incumbent leaders; the Apr 13 reading also follows Johnson's own COVID hospitalization.

events.event_summary: Hurricane Katrina slams into the Gulf Coast and the levees protecting New Orleans fail, flooding the city. Thousands are stranded on rooftops and in the Superdome for days as the federal relief effort stumbles amid scenes of chaos.
events.question: Will the public approve of President George W. Bush's job performance?
events.metric: % approving of President G.W. Bush's job performance
events.verification_note: Gallup monthly averages (news.gallup.com/poll/24283): Aug 43, Sep 44, Oct 41, Nov 38. Gallup's own headline: 'Little Impact of Katrina on Bush's Overall Job Ratings' — attribution is the weakest in this dataset; CNN/USAT/Gallup mid-Sept single reading was 40%.
events.notes: Kept as an anti-rally control but downgraded to low confidence: the slide is slow and partly attributable to Iraq/gas prices.

events.event_summary: A mob storms the United States Capitol to overturn the certification of the presidential election, battling police, ransacking offices, and forcing lawmakers to flee. Five people die in connection with the assault on the seat of Congress.
events.question: Will the public approve of President Donald Trump's job performance?
events.metric: % approving of President Trump's job performance
events.verification_note: Gallup (news.gallup.com/poll/328637): final reading 34%, 'down five points from Gallup's December poll' (=39). Corrected from authored 46->34 (46 was the pre-election Nov reading). Poll window began Jan 4 — straddles the event start.

events.event_summary: The new British government unveils a mini-budget of sweeping unfunded tax cuts. The pound crashes to a record low against the dollar, gilt markets seize up, and the Bank of England intervenes to stop pension funds from collapsing.
events.question: Will the governing Conservative Party be supported?
events.metric: % intending to vote Conservative
events.verification_note: YouGov published trackers: Con 28% (Sept 23-25) -> 21% (Sept 28-29, Labour +33 — largest lead since the 1990s). Both endpoints post-announcement; the window captures the market-meltdown reaction week. Last fully pre-budget YouGov (~32-33) not directly confirmed, so not used.

events.event_summary: A gunman murders twenty first-grade children and six educators at Sandy Hook Elementary School in Newtown, Connecticut, before killing himself. The massacre of six- and seven-year-olds stuns the country.
events.question: Will stricter laws covering the sale of firearms be supported?
events.poll_source: Gallup (laws covering the sale of firearms)
events.metric: % saying laws covering firearm sales should be made more strict
events.verification_note: USA Today/Gallup Dec 19-22 2012 (news.gallup.com/poll/159569): 58% favor stricter firearm-sale laws, up from 43% in 2011.
events.notes: Aligned case: negative event, support for the questioned policy rises — but note the question subject (stricter laws) benefits from negative event sentiment only if the mechanism understands the referent, which the sentiment-sign channel does not.

events.event_summary: A former student opens fire with a rifle at Marjory Stoneman Douglas High School in Parkland, Florida, killing seventeen students and staff. Surviving students launch a nationwide protest movement within days.
events.question: Will stricter laws covering the sale of firearms be supported?
events.poll_source: Gallup (laws covering the sale of firearms)
events.metric: % saying laws covering firearm sales should be made more strict
events.verification_note: Gallup (news.gallup.com/poll/229562 'Preference for Stricter Gun Laws Highest Since 1993'): 67% March 2018, +7pp vs October 2017.

events.event_summary: A draft Supreme Court opinion leaks showing the court is prepared to overturn Roe v. Wade and end the constitutional right to abortion. Protests erupt outside the court and across the country as states ready trigger bans.
events.question: Will legal access to abortion be supported?
events.metric: % identifying as pro-choice
events.verification_note: Gallup (news.gallup.com/poll/393104): pro-choice identification jumped six points to 55% in May 2022 (post-leak, pre-decision), from 49% the previous year.
events.notes: Threat-to-status-quo dynamic: support for the threatened right rises after a negative event about it.

events.event_summary: Russia launches a full-scale invasion of Ukraine, striking cities with missiles and pushing armored columns toward Kyiv. Europe's largest land war since 1945 begins on the doorstep of the Nordic states, and Finland's 1,300-kilometer border with Russia suddenly feels exposed.
events.question: Will joining the NATO military alliance be supported?
events.metric: % of Finns supporting NATO membership
events.verification_note: Taloustutkimus Jan 2022: 30% support (corrected from authored 28); Yle poll Mar 9-11 2022 (yle.fi/a/3-12357832): 62%. Support reached 76% by May (yle.fi/a/3-12437506).
events.notes: One of the largest, fastest documented opinion swings in modern polling; support kept climbing to ~76% by May 2022.

events.event_summary: Russia launches a full-scale invasion of Ukraine, striking cities with missiles and pushing armored columns toward Kyiv. The war shatters assumptions about European security and forces the historically non-aligned Nordic states to reconsider their defense posture.
events.question: Will joining the NATO military alliance be supported?
events.metric: % of Swedes supporting NATO membership
events.notes: AFTER endpoint confirmed (Novus 51% Apr 2022, first recorded majority, via The Local/Al Jazeera; mid-April Novus was 45%). January baseline 37 is authored and unconfirmed — hence verified stays false.

events.event_summary: Lehman Brothers files the largest bankruptcy in American history as the financial crisis explodes. Credit markets freeze, the government seizes AIG, and stock indexes suffer their worst crashes in decades while banks teeter worldwide.
events.question: Will consumers be confident about the economy?
events.poll_source: University of Michigan Index of Consumer Sentiment
events.metric: Michigan Index of Consumer Sentiment (index points)
events.verification_note: UMich ICS official table (sca.isr.umich.edu/files/tbmics.pdf): Sept 2008 70.3, Oct 2008 57.6.
events.notes: Metric is index points rather than percentage points; magnitude comparisons across events use rank correlation, so the unit difference is acceptable and is disclosed here.

events.event_summary: The World Health Organization declares the coronavirus outbreak a pandemic. Within days the United States bans travel from Europe, states order businesses closed, markets crash into bear territory, and millions face sudden layoffs.
events.question: Will consumers be confident about the economy?
events.poll_source: University of Michigan Index of Consumer Sentiment
events.metric: Michigan Index of Consumer Sentiment (index points)
events.verification_note: UMich ICS: Feb 2020 101.0 -> Apr 2020 71.8 (pandemic low; confirmed via Chicago Fed Letter 2023-490 + UMich tables).

events.event_summary: Chancellor Angela Merkel opens Germany's borders to hundreds of thousands of refugees stranded along the Balkan route. Arrivals surge past ten thousand a day; reception systems strain and a furious political backlash builds within her own coalition.
events.question: Will the public be satisfied with Chancellor Angela Merkel's performance?
events.metric: % satisfied with Merkel's work as Chancellor
events.verification_note: Infratest dimap via Bloomberg: satisfaction 'fell 9 percentage points to 54%' in Oct 2015 (=63 before), lowest since Dec 2011. Corrected from authored 67->54.
events.notes: Satisfaction kept falling to ~46% by early 2016.
